missions.title: A clearer responsibility limit
paragraphs: A customer asks an employee to approve an exception. The employee does not have authority to approve it. The people involved need enough information to choose a practical response.

To avoid further confusion, we decide to explain who can make the decision and pass on the request. The expected benefit is that the customer can reach the appropriate decision-maker. This gives the response a clear purpose that can be checked afterwards.

A useful decision takes account of the information available at the time. If an important detail changes, it may be sensible to review the plan. Explaining the reason for the decision helps other people understand when a different approach might be needed.

A polite boundary tells people what is possible without making an unclear promise. You can recognise that a request matters and still explain that you do not have time to complete it immediately. Offering a realistic alternative helps the other person make a plan. A clear answer is usually kinder than agreeing and then becoming unavailable.
In a similar conversation, you could say: “I can't take that on right now, but I can help tomorrow.” “Could it wait until Monday morning?” “Thanks for understanding. I'll reply during working hours.”
